h: The New Moon Renews Redemption Even in Exile

p: "He Who performed miracles for our fathers
and redeemed them from slavery to freedom,
what is the connection of this prayer for redemption
to the blessing of the new month?
It is as it was said
immediately at the redemption from Mitzrayim,
הַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם רֹאשׁ חֳדָשִׁים (שְׁמוֹת יב, ב)
"This month shall be for you the beginning of months" (Shemos 12:2);
and this is the first mitzvah that Yisrael were commanded
that Yisrael count by the renewal of the moon,
which has nothing of its own,
רַק מַה שֶּׁמֵּאִיר עָלָיו מֵאוֹר הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ
only what shines upon it from the light of the sun.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם מֵעַצְמָם שׁוּם כֹּחַ
That is, they have no power of their own,
only what He bestows upon them
וְהוּא עִנְיַן אָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת קנו, א)
And this is the matter of what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shabbos 156a):
and drinks what is not his
because he knows with certainty in his soul
that he has nothing of his own.
This is not so with the nations of the world,
one who eats of his own
שֶׁמְּדַמֶּה לוֹ שֶׁהַכֹּל מִכּוֹחוֹ וְעוֹצֶם יָדוֹ
for he imagines that everything is from his strength and the might of his hand.
וְזֶה הָיָה מִיָּד בְּרֵאשִׁית הַגְּאוּלָּה מִמִּצְרַיִם
And this was immediately at the beginning of the redemption from Mitzrayim;
an impression of the renewal of redemption is made
and saw that they recited Hallel on Rosh Chodesh;
כִּי כָּל הָאוֹמֵר הַלֵּל בְּכָל יוֹם
for whoever recites Hallel every day
only for redemption from every trouble,
וּמַה זֶּה עִנְיַן הַגְּאוּלָּה בְּרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ
so what is the connection of redemption to Rosh Chodesh?
But when he saw that they skipped parts,
the custom of their fathers is in their hands."
That is, specifically in the exile of Bavel
that there is an illumination of the renewal of redemption
to take refuge in His Providence, Yisbarach,
וְלֵידַע שֶׁכָּל הַנְהָגַת מַלְכֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם עִמָּנוּ
and to know that all the conduct of the kings of the nations toward us
is only from His power, Yisbarach.
And through this we can say,
And it is like what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (in Avos 3:5):
whoever accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah,
the yoke of government is removed from him;
that is, he knows in his soul
that everything is from His Providence, Yisbarach.
And about this we say in the blessing of the new month:
"He Who performed miracles for our fathers
and redeemed them from slavery to freedom"
in the first renewal, of the Exodus from Mitzrayim
even in every kind of distress and exile,
that everything is in His Providence, Yisbarach;
from the four corners of the earth, Amen."
